title: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, 4.6 Limits at Infinity and Asymptotes: Calculate the limit of a function as x increases or decreases without bound.
summary: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, 4.6 Limits at Infinity and Asymptotes: Calculate the limit of a function as x increases or decreases without bound.
body: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, section "4.6 Limits at Infinity and Asymptotes", prints these objectives: "Calculate the limit of a function as x increases or decreases without bound." "Recognize a horizontal asymptote on the graph of a function." "Estimate the end behavior of a function as x increases or decreases without bound." "Recognize an oblique asymptote on the graph of a function." "Analyze a function and its derivatives to draw its graph.". The section text says: "We have shown how to use the first and second derivatives of a function to describe the shape of a graph. To graph a function f defined on an unbounded domain, we also need to know the behavior of f as x → ± ∞ . In this section, we define limits at infinity and show how these limits affect the graph of a function. At the end of this section, we outline a strategy for graphing an arbitrary function f ." This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
